title: Part Seventeen: Without 1948: The Uganda Test and the Question of Legitimacy

sections.brief: Tests the argument that a Greater Israel programme presupposes 1948: every documented programme (1967 cabinet, Likud 1977, Golan Law, Nation-State Law, 2022 guidelines, 71-13 motion, 82% map) ran through state institutions; the idea preceded the state (1919 map, Revisionists 1925, Herut 1949-65) and no government adopted it before 1967; 1948 as contingent (two-thirds rule, 33-13-10 and the three-vote margin, 25-13-17 in committee, the 20-21 ICJ referral vote, US trusteeship retreat, the war), with two labelled readings. Figures: time; stats

The Uganda Test revisited (labelled argument), linking rd1 s04fa/s04e/s04f: Der Judenstaat on Argentina, El-Arish, the 1903 East Africa offer after Kishinev, 295-178-98 and the Russian walkout, 1905 rejection, the ITO to 1925, Birobidzhan 1928/1934 (never a Jewish majority), binationalism; which justifications travel (refuge, legal grant with its consent problem, self-determination only with a people present, not the historic claim); which 'Greater' claim could exist (no whole-land programme; buffer-zone expansion possible anywhere), with Israel's stated security rationale beside it. Figures: time; compare

Legitimacy arguments side by side, attributed: Israel's (1948 declaration, Mandate, 181, recognition, UN admission 37-12-9, self-determination, 1948 war) vs Palestinian/Arab and critics' (consent and Covenant Art. 22, 1947 objections and the 20-21 ICJ vote, population of the proposed state, the Nakba and refugee estimates, Resolution 194 and its two readings, 1968 Charter); the narrowing to the 1967 lines (1988 declaration, 1993 letters, treaties, 2002 Arab Peace Initiative, recognition counts); beyond the lines (242, 497, 2334, ICJ 2024 with votes, UNGA 2024) with Israel's rejection and the US/Colombia Golan exception. Figure: compare
